summary: Feed s183_triple is degraded for IDS: 3 faults. VLANs 10,20 required by IDS are completely missing (100% untagged), 8.6% of frames are sliced to ~192 bytes breaking full-payload inspection, and 74.8% encrypted share exceeds IDS tolerance of 60%.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN is stripping 802.1Q tags or feed is taken from untagged access ports. All packets arrive untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are never seen.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot apply VLAN-aware policies or segment detection for VLANs 10,20. Traffic from those segments is invisible or misclassified, creating complete detection blind spot for those VLANs.

recommended_fix.why: IDS profile requires VLANs 10,20 to be present. Configure broker to preserve 802.1Q tags end-to-end and ensure source TAPs are on trunk links carrying 10,20.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing/snaplen configured to ~192 bytes (153/1779 frames = 8.6% truncated, above 5% threshold). Likely intentional slicing to save tool bandwidth.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true. Sliced frames lose L7 payload, breaking signature matching, file extraction, and stream reassembly. IDS will miss payload-based detections.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload up to 1518 bytes. Disable slicing or increase snaplen to max_frame_bytes on broker egress to this IDS.

findings.root_cause: 74.8% of bytes are encrypted vs 60% IDS tolerance. Traffic is predominantly TLS/encrypted and is being sent to IDS without prior decryption or selective filtering.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is payload-dependent and cannot inspect encrypted payloads. High encrypted share blinds detection, reduces signature efficacy to metadata only, and wastes IDS capacity.

params.solution: out-of-band TLS decryption or selective forwarding

recommended_fix.why: Share exceeds tool tolerance. Decrypt relevant TLS centrally and forward cleartext to IDS, or filter/route encrypted traffic that IDS cannot analyze to maintain effective coverage.
